findings.issue_text: [High/bug] pkg/expr/reader.go:196-199 — `enableSqlExpressions` always returns `false` regardless of the feature flag state due to an inverted check (`enabled := !IsEnabledGlobally(...)`) followed by unconditional `return false`; should simply `return h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)`

[High/bug] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:8-25 — `DB` is a stub where every method returns `errors.New("not implemented")` but is wired into live code paths (`pkg/expr/sql_command.go:97` `QueryFramesInto` and `pkg/expr/sql/parser.go:24` `RunCommands` via `TablesList`), so any SQL expression that passes the feature gate always fails at runtime and `TablesList` (which has no gate) always errors — a functional regression versus the removed `go-duck` implementation

[Medium/bug] pkg/expr/sql_command.go:~1-15 — the diff replaces the `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck` import with no visible addition of the new `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql` import while the code calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB()`, which does not compile unless the import exists in unshown context; verify the import block

[Medium/api] pkg/expr/reader.go:130-132 — the error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is misleading since the actual cause is a disabled feature flag; it should reference the feature flag (e.g., "sqlExpressions feature is disabled") so operators can self-diagnose

[Medium/test_gap] pkg/expr/reader.go:193-200 — no tests are added for the new feature-gating behavior in `ReadQuery` (QueryTypeSQL with flag on/off) nor for the stub `pkg/expr/sql.DB` behavior, despite the gating logic containing an inverted-condition bug that tests would have caught

[Low/data] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:13,17,21 — errors are created inline with `errors.New("not implemented")` rather than exported sentinel errors (e.g., `ErrNotImplemented`), so callers cannot programmatically distinguish "not implemented" from other failures with `errors.Is`

[Low/doc_defect] pkg/expr/reader.go:193 — the function name `enableSqlExpressions` reads as an action but is a boolean predicate and should be named e.g. `sqlExpressionsEnabled`; the local variable `enabled` also shadows the negated flag check, obscuring the logic error

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] pkg/expr/sql_command.go:~1-15 — the diff replaces the `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck` import with no visible addition of the new `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql` import while the code calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB()`, which does not compile unless the import exists in unshown context; verify the import block

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql_command.go the diff removes the `github.com/scottlepp/go-duck/duck` import, but the updated code now calls `sql.NewInMemoryDB()` (`db := sql.NewInMemoryDB()`). In the shown import block snippet there is no corresponding new import for the `pkg/expr/sql` package (e.g., `"github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/expr/sql"`), so as shown this change would not compile due to an undefined `sql` identifier.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/api] pkg/expr/reader.go:130-132 — the error message "sqlExpressions is not implemented" is misleading since the actual cause is a disabled feature flag; it should reference the feature flag (e.g., "sqlExpressions feature is disabled") so operators can self-diagnose

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go the new QueryTypeSQL branch gates execution on `enabled := enableSqlExpressions(h)` and returns `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` when `!enabled`. This indicates the immediate reason for failure is the feature gate, not necessarily implementation status, so the finding that the error message is misleading is grounded in the diff. (Additionally, `enableSqlExpressions` currently returns false unconditionally, reinforcing that the path is effectively ‘disabled’.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] pkg/expr/reader.go:193-200 — no tests are added for the new feature-gating behavior in `ReadQuery` (QueryTypeSQL with flag on/off) nor for the stub `pkg/expr/sql.DB` behavior, despite the gating logic containing an inverted-condition bug that tests would have caught

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a real functional defect in the new SQL feature-gating: `enableSqlExpressions` (pkg/expr/reader.go) returns `false` on all paths. It sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` (inverting the meaning), then returns `false` both when `enabled` is true and at the end, so `ReadQuery` for `QueryTypeSQL` will always return `fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented")` regardless of flag state. This is a verifiable broken behavior introduced by the change (independent of whether tests were added).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] pkg/expr/sql/db.go:13,17,21 — errors are created inline with `errors.New("not implemented")` rather than exported sentinel errors (e.g., `ErrNotImplemented`), so callers cannot programmatically distinguish "not implemented" from other failures with `errors.Is`

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/sql/db.go the stub methods TablesList, RunCommands, and QueryFramesInto each return a freshly-created `errors.New("not implemented")`. Because these are distinct error instances, callers cannot reliably use `errors.Is(err, someErr)` to detect the specific "not implemented" condition unless a shared sentinel (e.g., `var ErrNotImplemented = errors.New(...)`) is introduced. This is a diff-grounded, actionable API/design concern rather than a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/expr/reader.go, enableSqlExpressions() is implemented to always return false: it sets `enabled := !h.features.IsEnabledGlobally(featuremgmt.FlagSqlExpressions)` and then returns false in both the `if enabled` branch and the default path. As a result, the new QueryTypeSQL path always errors with "sqlExpressions is not implemented" regardless of the feature flag state, which is a verifiable behavioral defect introduced by this diff. (The naming concern is secondary/style, but the logic error is real and grounded in the diff.)
